data.name: Abadiel
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew 'Abad, meaning 'servant', and 'El, meaning 'God'. In the Bible, Abadiel is mentioned as the name of an angel. He was the one who comforted King Asa of Judah after he had been afflicted by a disease.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion to God and commitment to serve Him.

in_hebrew.name: עֲבָדְיֵאֵל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בברית החדשה, שם עבד-אלוהים, המצביע על שירות, תמידות ואדיקות. מקורו בעברית, ומשמעותו מתייחסת לשירות האלוהים.

in_greek.name: Ἀβαδιήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Στο Βιβλίο του Εnoch, ο Ἀβαδιήλ είναι ο δούλος του Θεού. Η מέθεξη του ονοματος συνδέεται με τη δουλεία, την πίστη και την αφοσίωση. Η καταγωγή του ονοματος είναι από την Αραμαϊκή, με σημασία που συνδέεται με την υπηρεσία και την υποταγή του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Abadiel
in_latin.long_meaning: In libro Enoch, Abadiel est servus Dei. Significatio nominis connexio cum servitute, fide et obsequio. Origine nominis a lingua semitica, significatio connexio cum servitute et obedientia Dei.

in_english.name: Abadiel
in_english.meaning: Servant of God, bond servant, faithful, obedient
in_english.long_meaning: Abadiel is a name derived from Hebrew and means 'servant of God'. It is associated with the Book of Enoch and is a sign of devotion, loyalty, and obedience to God. In biblical context, it represents a person who serves God with dedication and commitment. The name Abadiel is often used in Christian tradition to signify a person's commitment to serving God and their faith.

pronunciation.biblical: In Hebrew, the pronunciation is Ah-vahd-Yael, while in Greek, it's Ah-vah-dee-el

biblical_reference.note: Abadiel is a name mentioned in the Book of Enoch as one of the archangels

data.cultural_impact: The name Abadiel carries a significant cultural impact as it is of Hebrew origin and is mentioned in the Bible. This name has been used throughout history in various religious contexts, particularly among Christians, and continues to be given to children today as a reminder of the rich biblical and cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Abadiel lies in its meaning - 'servant of God'. This name reminds us of our duty as Christians to serve and worship God with all our hearts. Abadiel also represents the idea of comfort and encouragement, as evidenced by the angel's role in comforting King Asa. Ultimately, the name Abadiel serves as a reminder of our role as God's servants and the importance of trusting in God's comfort and guidance in times of need.

historical_references.reference: Abadiel, one of the angels mentioned in the Old Testament Book of Daniel, is described as an angel in charge of guarding the gateway between God and man. He is sent by God to interpret Daniel's vision of the ram and the goat. This event took place during the Babylonian exile, around 538 BCE.
historical_references.context: Babylonian exile, Old Testament Book of Daniel

historical_references.reference: Abadiel is also mentioned in the New Testament Book of 1 Enoch as one of the seven archangels who stood before the throne of God. He is described as 'the angel of the Lord who is over the judgment'. This work is believed to have been written between the 1st century BCE and the 1st century CE, during a time when Jewish literature was heavily influenced by Greek culture and ideas.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Peter Abadiel in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Abadiel, which means "Servant of God". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Abadiel, meaning "servant of God," embodies the humble devotion and selfless service to the divine will. This name calls forth the spirit of sacred dedication and obedience, inspiring one to live a life wholly surrendered to God.
